[[CBE Hall of Fame Classic]] Champions |bowl =[[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = Round of 32 }} {{2013–14 Missouri Valley Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2013–14 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team''' represented [[Wichita State University]] in the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They played their home games at [[Charles Koch Arena]], which had a capacity of 10,506.{{cite web |title = Koch Arena |url = http://www.goshockers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=7500&ATCLID=613212 |url-status = dead |archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20141024075111/http://www.goshockers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=7500&ATCLID=613212 |archivedate = 2014-10-24 }} They were in their 69th season as a member of the [[Missouri Valley Conference]]. They were led by seventh-year head coach [[Gregg Marshall]]. They were the last team to finish the regular season and enter the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] unbeaten until [[2014-15 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] did it the next year. == Description == The 2013–14 season was arguably the best season in Wichita State's 108-year basketball history. After defeating [[2013–14 Missouri State Bears men's basketball team|Missouri State]] on March 1, 2014, Wichita State became the first men's Division I team ever to finish the regular season 31–0 ([[2014-15 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] matched it the next year),{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400500140|title=No. 2 Wichita State finishes perfect regular season with rout|access-date=2014-03-02|date=2014-03-01|agency=[[Associated Press]] |publisher=[[ESPN]]}} the first team to finish 18–0 in conference play in the Missouri Valley Conference since the [[1985–86 Bradley Braves men's basketball team|1985–86 Bradley Braves]], as well as the first to finish the regular season undefeated since [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's]] in [[2003–04 Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball team|2003–04]]. The team's 35–0 start was the best men's Division I start ever (before Kentucky started 38–0 the next year), beating the [[1990–91 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team|1990–91 UNLV Runnin' Rebels]] who began the season 34–0 and the best Missouri Valley Conference start ever, beating the [[1978–79 Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball team|1978–79 Indiana State Sycamores]], who went 33–0 to start the season. They spent most of the season in the top 10 of both major polls, rising as high as #2 in late February. They continued their run by winning their first [[2014 Missouri Valley Conference men's basketball tournament|MVC tournament title]] since 1987, and were ranked second in both final major media polls, the highest final national ranking in school history. However, some analysts noted that Wichita State's schedule was relatively easy compared to previous teams that finished the regular season primarily because none of their opponents throughout the season were ranked when they played them, as well as only beating one opponent that was ranked at any point in the season (Saint Louis, who also had a lack of quality wins).{{cite web |title=How Impressive Is Wichita State's Undefeated 2013-14 Regular Season? |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1978150-how-impressive-is-wichita-states-undefeated-2013-14-regular-season |website=BleacherReport.com}} They entered the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] undefeated at 34–0. The Shockers beat [[2013-14 Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball team|Cal Poly]], 64–37. Two days later, and playing their 5th and final straight game at [[St. Louis]]' [[Scottrade Center]], [[Fred VanVleet]]'s three-point attempt at the end-of-game buzzer against [[2013-14 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] bounced harmlessly off the rim, and so went their attempt to become the first men's team in 38 years to win the title undefeated. ==Preseason== In the 2012–13 college basketball season, the Wichita State University Shockers, under sixth-year head coach Gregg Marshall, finished the season 30–9 and 12–6 in Missouri Valley play to finish in second place. They advanced to the championship game of the Missouri Valley Tournament where they lost to Creighton. They received an at-large bid to the 2013 NCAA Tournament, receiving a 9 seed in the West Region, where they defeated 8 seed Pittsburgh and 1 seed Gonzaga to advance to the Sweet Sixteen. In the West Region semifinals, they defeated 13 seed La Salle and 2 seed Ohio State in the regional finals to be crowned West Region Champions and advance to the Final Four for the second time in school history and first time since 1965. In the Final Four, they lost to eventual-champion Louisville, 72–68. Wichita State was ranked #4 in the final Coach's Poll of the 2012–13 season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2013/4/9/4205512/college-basketball-rankings-coaches-poll-top-25-louisville-wichita-state|title = Louisville tops Coaches Poll|date = 9 April 2013}} ==Departures== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
